momentum-conservation.title: Momentum Conservation
momentum-conservation.intro: Apply conservation of linear momentum to find the final velocity of a system when no external force acts, such as in a collision.

en.title: Momentum Conservation
en.intro: Apply conservation of linear momentum to find the final velocity of a system when no external force acts, such as in a collision.

elastic-collision-1d.title: 1D Elastic Collision
elastic-collision-1d.intro: Solve a one-dimensional perfectly elastic collision for the final velocities of both masses, where both momentum and kinetic energy are conserved.

en.title: 1D Elastic Collision
en.intro: Solve a one-dimensional perfectly elastic collision for the final velocities of both masses, where both momentum and kinetic energy are conserved.

impulse.title: Impulse
impulse.intro: Calculate impulse as the product of force and time, equal to the change in linear momentum it produces.

en.title: Impulse
en.intro: Calculate impulse as the product of force and time, equal to the change in linear momentum it produces.

torque-force.title: Torque from Force
torque-force.intro: Calculate torque (moment of force) from the applied force, lever-arm length, and the angle between them.

en.title: Torque from Force
en.intro: Calculate torque (moment of force) from the applied force, lever-arm length, and the angle between them.

power-force.title: Power from Force
power-force.intro: Calculate mechanical power delivered by a force moving an object at a given velocity (power = force × velocity).

en.title: Power from Force
en.intro: Calculate mechanical power delivered by a force moving an object at a given velocity (power = force × velocity).

kinetic-friction.title: Kinetic Friction
kinetic-friction.intro: Compute the kinetic friction force opposing sliding motion from the coefficient of kinetic friction and the normal force.

en.title: Kinetic Friction
en.intro: Compute the kinetic friction force opposing sliding motion from the coefficient of kinetic friction and the normal force.

work-energy-theorem.title: Work-Energy Theorem
work-energy-theorem.intro: Apply the work-energy theorem: the net work done on an object equals its change in kinetic energy.

en.title: Work-Energy Theorem
en.intro: Apply the work-energy theorem: the net work done on an object equals its change in kinetic energy.

momentum.title: Momentum
momentum.intro: Compute linear momentum as the product of an object's mass and velocity — a vector quantity central to collision analysis.

en.title: Momentum
en.intro: Compute linear momentum as the product of an object's mass and velocity — a vector quantity central to collision analysis.

period-pendulum.title: Pendulum Period
period-pendulum.intro: Find the period of a simple pendulum from its length and the local gravitational acceleration using the small-angle approximation.

en.title: Pendulum Period
en.intro: Find the period of a simple pendulum from its length and the local gravitational acceleration using the small-angle approximation.

inelastic-collision.title: Inelastic Collision
inelastic-collision.intro: Find the common final velocity after a perfectly inelastic collision in which two objects stick together and kinetic energy is not conserved.

en.title: Inelastic Collision
en.intro: Find the common final velocity after a perfectly inelastic collision in which two objects stick together and kinetic energy is not conserved.

banked-curve.title: Banked Curve Speed
banked-curve.intro: Find the frictionless design speed for a banked curve from its radius and banking angle, where the horizontal component of the normal force supplies the centripetal force.

en.title: Banked Curve Speed
en.intro: Find the frictionless design speed for a banked curve from its radius and banking angle, where the horizontal component of the normal force supplies the centripetal force.

hooke-force.title: Hooke's Law Force
hooke-force.intro: Apply Hooke's law to find the restoring force of a spring from its stiffness (spring constant) and displacement from equilibrium.

en.title: Hooke's Law Force
en.intro: Apply Hooke's law to find the restoring force of a spring from its stiffness (spring constant) and displacement from equilibrium.

spring-potential.title: Spring Potential Energy
spring-potential.intro: Compute the elastic potential energy stored in a compressed or stretched spring from its stiffness and displacement.

en.title: Spring Potential Energy
en.intro: Compute the elastic potential energy stored in a compressed or stretched spring from its stiffness and displacement.

coefficient-restitution.title: Coefficient of Restitution
coefficient-restitution.intro: Determine the coefficient of restitution between two colliding objects from their approaching and separating velocities — a measure of how elastic (bouncy) the impact is.

en.title: Coefficient of Restitution
en.intro: Determine the coefficient of restitution between two colliding objects from their approaching and separating velocities — a measure of how elastic (bouncy) the impact is.

inclined-plane-accel.title: Inclined Plane Acceleration

en.intro: Compute the acceleration of an object sliding down an inclined plane, accounting for gravity, the slope angle, and kinetic friction.

power-rotational.title: Rotational Power

static-friction-max.title: Maximum Static Friction
static-friction-max.intro: Determine the maximum static friction force that can act before an object begins to slide, from the coefficient of static friction and the normal force.

terminal-velocity.title: Terminal Velocity

angular-momentum-conservation.title: Angular Momentum Conservation

angular-momentum.title: Angular Momentum

moment-of-inertia-point.title: Point Mass Moment of Inertia

rotational-kinetic-energy.title: Rotational Kinetic Energy

en.title: Rotational Kinetic Energy
en.intro: Find the kinetic energy stored in a rotating body from its moment of inertia and angular velocity.

weight-force.title: Weight Force
weight-force.intro: Compute an object's weight (gravitational force) from its mass and the local gravitational acceleration.

en.title: Weight Force
